name: Ally Aiken Design
line: Watercolour golf course maps from Austin — hundreds of courses, commissions open.

name: Artisan Golf
line: Two ex-Nike craftsmen in Nike's old Fort Worth building — wedges ground by hand, fitting required.

name: Aug 11
line: Hat brand founded in 2023 by Johnny Person — rope caps and buckets with a vintage Southern lean.

name: AustinKnittyLimits
line: Hand-knit retro headcovers from Austin, one at a time, taught by the maker's mother.

name: BEAMS Golf
line: The golf line of Tokyo's BEAMS empire, running since 2011 — Japanese fairway fashion at its most complete.

name: BestGrips
line: A father and son making leather grips in Texas — Horween leathers, no minimums, no paid endorsements.

name: Big Dog Golf Co.
line: Leather covers stocked in the pro shops at Royal Melbourne, Barnbougle and Cape Wickham.

name: Birds of Condor
line: Byron Bay's cult label — started with ten hats, now a flagship store with a restored 80s buggy inside.

name: Bluetross
line: Horween and Italian leather covers, belts and wallets, co-founded by Gail Hanson.

name: Bunker Mentality
line: Twenty-plus years independent, co-founded by Tamasine Green; now cut made-to-order with no warehouse.

name: Casualist
line: Elie Reboul's West London label that outgrew its own name — quiet clothes for golf and after.

name: Chipp Golf Co
line: Cabretta gloves with a conscience — ten per cent of every glove goes to a charitable partner.

name: Clint Orms
line: Hill Country silversmith, est. 1992 — sterling ball markers, never more than ten from one design.

name: Cloud & Wind Golf
line: Grips only — Eastern aesthetics, Chinese verse printed on the box, $18 a grip.

name: Criquet Shirts
line: Austin's original players shirt, est. 2010 — Pima cotton, removable stays, made in Peru and says so.

name: Daphne's Headcovers
line: Founded 1979 by Jane Spicer and her mother. Made Frank, the tiger headcover Tiger Woods carried.

name: Devant Sport Towels
line: Founded 1976 by Mary Ann Sheppard. Licensed towels for the USGA, PGA of America, PGA Tour and LPGA.

name: Devereux Golf
line: Scottsdale brothers, est. 2013, named after their grandfather — relaxed silhouettes before that was normal.

name: Duca del Cosma
line: Italian golf shoes co-founded in 2004 by Antje Elle and Baldovino Mattiazzo; since sold twice.

name: Edel Golf
line: David Edel's putters, fitted like irons and still hand-finished in Austin.

name: Edison Golf
line: Terry Koehler's wedge company on the Gulf Coast — the patented Koehler Sole, built to order.

name: Fella Golf
line: Tongue-in-cheek European golf — heavyweight tees, a pizza-slice ball marker, zero seriousness.

name: Found Golf
line: Half gallery, half golf label — Melbourne's Lance Peach and Ellen Keillar sell paintings next to polos.

name: Fyfe Golf
line: Putter covers in sail cloth, marine suede and waxed canvas — plus the MacKenzie editions.

name: Gramicci
line: Climbing pants born on Yosemite granite in 1982 that quietly became golf-course staples.

name: Gray + Haast
line: Named for the founder and the largest eagle that ever lived — clean Queensland golfwear.

name: Gumtree Nature Club
line: Nature-first golf goods from Australia — the drop that sold on gum leaves and gravel car parks.

name: Hedge
line: Meagan Ouderkirk and Antonia DiPaolo's golf and tennis label — and the only people in golf making a caddie brooch.

name: Huega House
line: Carlsbad, est. 2022 — retro-modern prints, towels and objects that treat golf as graphic design.

name: Inside Story Socks
line: Golf socks knit from coffee grounds and recycled bottles, co-founded by Isabelle Shee.

name: Jan Craig Headcovers
line: Hand-knit wool headcovers since 1962. Nicklaus, Watson and Ryder Cup teams carried them.

name: Jones Sports Co
line: The 1971 carry bag that never went away — revived in Portland and better than the original.

name: Juniper & James
line: From the founder of Duck Camp, named for his twins — breathable polos for Hill Country heat.

name: Kingfisher Golf
line: Started at a kitchen counter in East Dallas by a former PepsiCo art director; first athlete signed via a Worst Golfer in Dallas contest.

name: Lamb Crafted
line: A six-person Texas machine shop — engraved putters, markers and leather from Tyson Lamb's bench.

name: Left of Field Golf
line: Surf and skate silhouettes for the course, every collection named for a stretch of Australian coast.

name: Mackem Golf
line: Wool headcovers sewn in the Perth hills — bespoke work from football shirts and family tartan.

name: Malbon Golf
line: Co-founded 2017 by Erica and Stephen Malbon. Started as an Instagram mood board.

name: Manors Golf
line: London's modern-heritage benchmark — and the Reebok collab that sold through twice.

name: Merrill Golf
line: A design venture through the lens of golf — acid-washed tees, heavyweight fleece and a flying duck.

name: Metalwood Studio
line: Cole Young's LA studio mining Y2K tour aesthetics — the blueprint for modern golf nostalgia.

name: Midiron
line: Nine products, no founder named, everything shot at night on a floodlit par-three.

name: Mogshade
line: Handmade Portuguese headcovers and towels, made to order on a three-week lead.

name: Morning People Clothiers
line: Designed in the USA, sewn in South Korea — early-tee-time clothes with a five-piece discipline.

name: Odd Ritual
line: Born in Cape Town, named for the small habits before every shot — golf without the gatekeeping.

name: Okka Golf
line: Screen-printed by one person in Perth who refuses wholesale on principle.

name: Olydoe
line: An ex-banker's anti-polyester manifesto — Supima cotton polos, launched October 2025.

name: ORKAI
line: Formerly ORCA Golf. Founded by Deborah and Erica Bennett; bag supplier to the 2023 LPGA International Crown.

name: P53 Irons
line: Named for Hogan's 1953 season — American-forged irons finished in Fort Worth, by invitation.

name: Penta Golf
line: Three unnamed friends from magazine publishing — golf clothes with an art department's eye.

name: Piretti Putters
line: Milled from solid billets since 2008 — heavier heads, 2.5 degrees of loft, no cast putters ever.

name: PUMA Golf
line: COBRA PUMA GOLF's apparel and footwear arm — and the big brand most willing to take a swing at a collab.

name: Quiet Golf
line: From the Museum of Peace & Quiet orbit — considered golf clothes with an owl crest and an adidas Samba collab.

name: Radry Golf
line: A Wisconsin artist whose logo is a bird in a bucket hat — est. 2018, drawn before it is stitched.

name: Random Golf Club
line: Erik Anders Lang's community that became a brand — meetups, films, and the only Australia trip in golf media.

name: Read The Green
line: New York energy, est. 1997 graphics — the '97 nylon pullover is the piece that went viral.

name: Realtree
line: The camouflage licensor turning forty, now with golf collabs at PUMA and Sun Mountain.

name: Rhoback
line: Performance polos out of UVA's Darden incubator, co-founded by Kristina Loftus.

name: Rouqe Golf
line: Mock necks and retro rugby stripes, shot on a dry mountain course. Founder not publicly named.

name: Royal Albartross
line: Luxury golf footwear made in Italy and Portugal, founded by designer Alex Bartholomew.

name: Seamus Golf
line: Hand-cut wool headcovers and blacksmith-hammered markers from a Beaverton workshop that covered the 2016 U.S. Ryder Cup team.

name: Sentinel Golf
line: Minneapolis walker bags from $810 — Dyneema, Danish textiles, and no interest in compromise.

name: Siegelman Stable
line: Max Siegelman's NYC stable — racing-heritage sweats that ended up on tour players and a Maxfli box.

name: Sierra Madre Golf
line: Women's golf clothes by two women who play — built-in bras, real pockets, a glove loop on the skort.

name: Sinking Birdies
line: Bold-print Cabretta gloves, towels and covers. Co-founder Christina Rogers verified via Companies House.

name: Students Golf
line: Campus-inflected golfwear built on varsity graphics and a deep bench of collabs.

name: Sugarloaf Social Club
line: The group chat that became a brand — Ian Gilley's crew, est. 2011, sailing capsules and hidden gems.

name: Sun Mountain
line: Invented the modern stand bag in 1986 and the folding push cart in 1999; still assembles its bags in Montana.

name: Takomo Golf
line: Finnish direct-to-consumer irons, est. 2021 — tour-quality forgings at half the shop price.

name: TwentyFour Golf
line: Small-batch Australian covers and accessories, twelve pieces at a time.

name: Walker Golf Things
line: Pro skater Jack Fardell's label — named after Nicklaus, collabs with adidas, Wahine and Coopers.

name: Zalea's Golf Co.
line: Zoe Walker-Faure's hand-sewn headcovers, started in a college dorm with her mother and grandmother.
